title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 21 (Authentication of documents, proceedings and contracts)

content.overview: Section 21 provides that, save as otherwise provided in the Act, (a) a document or proceeding requiring authentication by a company, or (b) contracts made by or on behalf of a company, may be signed by any key managerial personnel or an officer or employee of the company duly authorised by the Board in this behalf.
content.glance: Authentication of company documents, proceedings and contracts by KMP or Board-authorised officer or employee.
content.study: Save as otherwise provided in the Act, a document or proceeding requiring authentication by a company, or any contract made by or on behalf of a company, may be signed by any key managerial personnel or an officer or employee of the company duly authorised by the Board in this behalf. The words “or employee” were added by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017. Current-law framing: identify the document, proceeding or contract; confirm the signatory is KMP or a Board-authorised officer or employee; apply any special authentication rule elsewhere in the Act if it overrides section 21.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Documents or proceedings requiring authentication by a company, and contracts made by or on behalf of a company.

sections.heading: Who may sign
sections.body: Any key managerial personnel, or an officer or employee of the company duly authorised by the Board in this behalf.

sections.heading: Saving clause
sections.body: Section 21 applies save as otherwise provided in the Act — special authentication rules elsewhere prevail where they apply.

provisions.title: Authentication of documents, proceedings and contracts

examples.title: KMP authentication
examples.body: The company secretary signs a return requiring authentication. Section 21 is satisfied if the CS is KMP.

examples.title: Board-authorised employee
examples.body: An employee signs a contract under a Board resolution authorising that employee for contracts of that class. Section 21 is satisfied.

hypotheticals.question: Can any employee sign company contracts without Board authority?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. An officer or employee may sign only if duly authorised by the Board. KMP may sign under the section without a separate authorisation for authentication purposes.

distinctions.title: Authentication (s. 21) vs execution of bills/deeds (s. 22)
distinctions.left: Who may authenticate documents, proceedings and contracts
distinctions.right: How bills, notes and attorney deeds bind the company

rows.left: Signing authority for authentication and contracts

misconceptions.trap: Only directors can authenticate company documents.
misconceptions.correction: Section 21 permits any KMP or a Board-authorised officer or employee.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 21 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the document, proceeding or contract. II. Check whether a special rule elsewhere in the Act applies. III. Confirm signature by KMP or Board-authorised officer/employee. IV. Conclude.
